title: Why All-Nighters Wreck Your Memory the Next Day
description:
Pulling an all-nighter doesn't just make you tired. Here's what's actually happening to your memory while you skip sleep.

Educational content, not medical advice.

#shorts #wellbeing #sleepfacts

scenes.text: Skipping a full night of sleep doesn't just make you tired. It changes how your brain handles what you just learned.
During deep sleep, the brain replays the day's experiences, moving them from short-term into longer-term storage.
Researchers call this memory consolidation, and it happens mainly in specific sleep stages you only get with real, uninterrupted sleep.
Pull an all-nighter, and that replay process gets cut short, so the information never fully locks in.
That's part of why cramming right before a test often backfires, even if it feels productive in the moment.
Sleep researchers generally agree that a full night of sleep after learning something new does more for retention than extra study time.
